facts.statement: Fossils of Scythosuchus were discovered in Lower Triassic rock layers in Russia.
facts.quote: Remains have been found from Olenekian-age Lower Triassic beds in Russia

facts.statement: The name Scythosuchus translates to 'Scythian crocodile'.
The genus Scythosuchus was described by Sennikov in 1999.
Scythosuchus basileus is the only known species in the genus.
facts.quote: The type and only species is S. basileus

facts.statement: Scythosuchus grew to be between 2 and 3 meters long and had a heavy build.
facts.quote: Scythosuchus was between 2 and 3 metres long, and relatively heavily built

facts.statement: Scythosuchus is classified as an extinct genus of rauisuchid.
facts.quote: Scythosuchus is an extinct genus of rauisuchid

facts.statement: Scythosuchus belongs to the family Rauisuchidae.
The parent group of Scythosuchus is Vjushkovisaurini.
Scythosuchus possessed blade-like, serrated teeth with a backward curve adapted for slicing flesh.
facts.quote: The blade-like teeth are laterally compressed and serrated, with a slight backwards curve, and would have been excellent for slicing through flesh

facts.statement: The dental structure indicates that Scythosuchus was a carnivore.
facts.quote: clearly indicating that Scythosuchus was a carnivore like other rauisuchids

facts.statement: The thick lower jaw with expanded articular areas suggests Scythosuchus had a powerful bite.
facts.quote: The lower jaw is thick and has very expanded articular areas, possibly indicating a powerful bite

facts.statement: The cervical vertebrae of Scythosuchus had low, poorly developed neural spines with thickened tips that made them top-heavy.
facts.quote: the neural spines are also very low and poorly developed, with a slightly widened and thickened tip making them top-heavy

facts.statement: Moving down the spine, the neural spines of Scythosuchus became thicker, heavier, and more rugose, resembling osteoderms.
facts.quote: As the vertebrae move back from the skull, the neural spines grow thicker, heavier and more rugose at the dorsal ends until they resemble osteoderms

facts.statement: The femur of Scythosuchus is well known from multiple specimens and has a sigmoidal shape with weak lateral compression.
facts.quote: The femur is much better known, as several specimens have been found, and was sigmoidal with weak lateral compression

facts.statement: Sennikov (2022) proposed that Scythosuchus might be synonymous with Tsylmosuchus donensis.
facts.quote: Sennikov (2022) suggested that Scythosuchus may be synonymous with Tsylmosuchus donensis

facts.statement: Ezcuraa et al. (2023) reclassified Tsylmosuchus as a proterosuchid rather than a pseudosuchian, countering the synonymy hypothesis.
facts.quote: but Ezcuraa et al. (2023) reclassified Tsylmosuchus as a proterosuchid instead of a pseudosuchian

rejected.statement: The shape of the calcaneum suggests Scythosuchus had an ankle joint intermediate between thecodonts and crocodilians.
rejected.quote: The overall shape of the calcaneum indicates an ankle joint intermediate between thecodonts and crocodilians
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'an ankle joint intermediate between thecodonts and crocodilians'
